entry_conditions: Can take over during any supported portion of the assigned expanded slices: open-finger source approach, close/lift, held carry/lower, closed-held goal entry, partial opening, settling, or empty retreat/next approach. Use causal world-frame observations: qpos[7:9] gives per-finger metres, qvel[16:18] gives finger velocities, tcp_pose[18:25] and red_pose[25:32]/blue_pose[32:39] give XYZ metres and wxyz quaternions, and goals[41:47] identify separate regions. Supply the two most recent observation frames, or repeat the current frame for a cold start. Measured expanded entries have fingers near 0.04 m each and TCP z approximately 0.088-0.178 m; these ranges are evidence, not hard applicability gates. A closed nearby cube may still be the payload even if its containment predicate is true. The policy infers intended/pending roles from observations; the runtime does not accept external role tokens or past-action history.
exit_conditions: Report formal contract success separately from empty-hand readiness. Contract truth requires both rotated cubes contained in their marked XY regions and centers within 0.011 m of goal z=0.036 m, with no release, clearance, velocity or hold requirement. For a reusable empty-hand exit, observations should support fingers opening toward 0.04 m each, a settled cube around z=0.036 m and separation of TCP motion from the placed object. The red useful demonstrated endpoint is an empty open approach above blue at TCP z about 0.267 m; final blue useful endpoints are open retreat/hold near z=0.3165 m. A caller can stop earlier on task success but must not claim that an attached or still-opening state is already an empty-hand acquisition exit.
overlap_role: This delivery model trains on every action in all 24 unchanged expanded slices. It learns incoming source approach, close/lift/carry as well as the outgoing pre-release lower, held containment, opening transient, settling, vertical retreat and red-to-blue open approach. The measured acquire_block overlaps include demo10300 [75,182), [265,415), [445,562) and demo10307 [72,178), [259,408), [439,552). At demo10300 265 the red cube remains held near z=0.112 m; at demo10307 259 it remains held near z=0.123 m. An early successor requesting blue may therefore inherit held red rather than an empty hand. This model's observation-conditioned belief preserves likely held identity in its training labels, and its diffusion decoder learns to complete the transition rather than switching solely on a goal flag.
successor_readiness: An acquisition successor should receive the actual causal observation history plus caller-maintained intended/pending identity if its own interface supports it, and separate descriptions of containment, likely attachment and disengagement. The present model has inferred role probabilities and separate belief heads, available through an optional beliefs method, but the standard framework forwards only epsilon/actions and does not automatically transport these diagnostics or a persistent hidden state. Assess aperture and relative TCP/object motion directly when diagnostics are unavailable. Demo10300 280 has contained red at z=0.04574 m and fingers near 0.0183 m with command -1; it is not an empty-hand state. At 290 fingers are about 0.0371 m, red is settled at z=0.036 m, and TCP remains near z=0.0453 m: partial opening is supported, but retreat still remains. Later, object persistence while TCP rises supports disengagement. These are inferred contact/readiness cues, not measured contact or proof of safety.
failure_signatures: Treat goal-true plus cube rising with retreat as evidence against disengagement. Open commands with fingers remaining near grasp width, re-closing after opening, a placed cube leaving containment, premature payload switching, or repeated belief changes driven only by noisy finger qvel are concerning. Fingers can have nonzero opposing qvel while remaining near a stable grasp width, so aperture change and TCP/object displacement are stronger combined evidence than a velocity sign alone. The learned readiness and persistence losses target these distinctions, but the training data contain successful examples, not sustained stiction, bounce-out or failed regrasp; reliable recovery under these signatures is untested.
continuation_guidance: If manipulation continuity matters and a cube still follows the TCP or the fingers remain at grasp width, continue this policy through the supported lower/open/settle transition, or transfer only to a successor explicitly capable of continuing that same phase. Do not transfer with an instruction to close immediately on blue merely because red_at_goal became true. During demonstrated detached retreat and approach, preserve the +1 open branch. After the red object is placed and decoupled, the learned continuation approaches blue openly; after final blue placement it learns open retreat/hold. The caller may terminate immediately on formal task success instead. Execution is fixed at eight actions per framework chunk; the research suggestion of adaptive 1-2-step replanning near release is not implemented. No fixed dwell, elapsed-time phase switch or extra velocity threshold is imposed by this package.
limitations: The recurrent belief spans only the two provided frames and is reinitialized for every forward pass; it is not an eight-frame or cross-invocation latch. Missing-history duplication is trained, but arbitrary missing information and arbitrary requested roles are not recoverable. Beliefs are weakly supervised probabilistic estimates, and readiness labels use future trajectories only during training. Only successful releases provide evidence. Shared normalizer scales are fitted on complete original demonstrations, not these slices. No scripted controller, replay, IK, hard obstacle constraint, image model or geometric action equivariance is implemented. The numerical package checks do not measure task performance or validate the handoff hypothesis.
